articles.title: It works on my machine" and other lies we tell our DevOps team
articles.excerpt: There is no sentence in the tech industry that triggers a DevOps engineer faster than: "Well, it works fine on my local machine." We have all done it. The build fails in production, the pipeline is sc…
articles.body: There is no sentence in the tech industry that triggers a DevOps engineer faster than: "Well, it works fine on my local machine." We have all done it. The build fails in production, the pipeline is screaming in bright red, the client is panicking, and the developer is sitting there calmly spinning containers locally without a single error. The gap between a local environment and staging is where engineering sanity goes to die. It’s usually a hidden environment variable, a slight version mismatch in a package, or pure dark magic. As we head into the weekend, what is the most ridiculous "local machine" bug that completely broke your production environment this week? Let's share some deployment trauma in the comments. P.S.
articles.author: Juliqn Stonov

articles.title: SlothSort: A Local AI Assistant for the Downloads Folder
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady SlothSort helps tidy a folder without the tedious drag-and-drop routine. It looks at filenames, asks a local…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady What I Built SlothSort helps tidy a folder without the tedious drag-and-drop routine. It looks at filenames, asks a local AI model to suggest categories and clearer names, and presents the proposed moves for review. Files are only moved after the user confirms the plan. Demo The project currently runs locally. Install the dependencies and follow the Ollama setup in the README . There is no public demo yet. Code View the source code on GitHub. How I Built It The interface uses Streamlit, and the app asks a local Ollama server to run the open-weight qwen2.5:3b model. The model sees filenames only and returns a category plus a suggested name.

articles.title: The Eight-Day Gap: Patch, Disclosure and Exposure in the BeyondTrust Zero-Day
articles.excerpt: The Eight-Day Gap: Patch, Disclosure and Exposure in the BeyondTrust Zero-Day Two dates in the BeyondTrust record decide who has a problem. The vendor fixed CVE-2026-102764 for SaaS customers on 8 Oct…
articles.body: The Eight-Day Gap: Patch, Disclosure and Exposure in the BeyondTrust Zero-Day Two dates in the BeyondTrust record decide who has a problem. The vendor fixed CVE-2026-102764 for SaaS customers on 8 October 2026. It disclosed the flaw on 15 October 2026, a week later, after Mandiant and Google had already watched Armory Castle exploit it against appliances since late August. That ordering is normal for a zero-day. It is also the reason patching statistics alone rarely answer the question security teams are actually asked, which is whether anything was reachable while the flaw was live and unannounced. What happened inside the window BeyondTrust describes CVE-2026-102764 as an authentication bypass, rated 9.3, affecting Remote Support 26.2.3 and earlier.

articles.body: Namespace design: for production workloads Scale converts an informal convention into an outage mechanism. For namespace design for production workloads , the decisive question is not whether a team can demonstrate the technology once. It is whether the organisation can operate it repeatedly, audit its decisions, and recover when assumptions fail. The operating problem Treat namespace design as part of a multi-tenant Kubernetes platform with declarative reconciliation and bounded workload privileges. Define the consumer, owner, support boundary, change policy, and recovery objective before selecting implementation details. When operating namespace design for production workloads, undocumented authority and ambiguous ownership create more risk than a missing feature.

articles.body: AI disclosure: An AI agent prepared this article by reading an existing Python CLI. The command combinations are hypothetical inspection cases, not executed tests. No product recommendation, commercial link or measured API result is included. A command-line parser can accept an option even when the selected execution branch never uses it. To understand an unfamiliar CLI, inspect both the argument definitions and the code that consumes the resulting namespace. The Python example examined here has three mutually exclusive mode flags: --demo , --live and --list-models . It also accepts --ticket , --model and --output . Those definitions describe the command's vocabulary. They do not, by themselves, describe every meaningful combination.

articles.title: 'Stupendously large black holes' aren't a major component of dark matter, study finds
articles.excerpt: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of dark matter, the mysterious stuff that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds.
articles.body: Black holes more massive than entire galaxies are not a major component of the mysterious dark matter that's thought to make up most of the matter in the cosmos, a new study finds. For decades, to explain why galaxies do not spin apart at the speeds at which they whirl, scientists have suggested the existence of an unseen substance known as dark matter , whose gravitational pull helps keep galaxies together. Dark matter is thought to make up about five-sixths of all matter in the universe . Much remains unknown about dark matter, however — including whether or not it actually exists. Black holes make good potential contenders for dark matter, since they are extremely massive and are difficult to spot in the dark depths of space.

articles.body: The Call of Duty matchmaking debate has raged on pretty much since the beginning of multiplayer. Should matches be comprised of evenly skilled players, if there’s an accurate enough way of ensuring that? Or should skill be stripped out of the equation, so you never know what to expect from the next match? Both sides of the argument have their valid reasons for their preference, but most recently, in 2025’s Black Ops 7, an option was presented that attempted to satisfy all. While the default matchmaking was set to skill-based, as has been the case since 2007’s game-changing Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, open matchmaking playlists were also available to those who want the opportunity to get teamed up with, and against, anybody.

articles.body: Rocket Lab launched a trio of private signals-intelligence satellites to orbit today (Oct. 23). The mission lifted off aboard an Electron rocket from Rocket Lab’s New Zealand launch site today at 3:11 a.m. EDT (0711 GMT; 8:11 p.m. local time in New Zealand). The Electron carried three "Hawk" satellites for the Virginia-based company HawkEye 360, which explains the name Rocket Lab gave to the mission: "We're Not Hawking Around." If all goes according to plan, the three Hawks will be deployed into low Earth orbit (LEO), at an altitude of 323 miles (520 kilometers). Once up there and commissioned, the satellites will scan the globe for radio frequency (RF) emissions.

articles.title: Space debris: Are we on track for true sustainability? (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: Space is a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. It’s therefore critical to maintain a safe and clean orbital environment.
articles.body: David Zamora is the chairman of the Space Data Association. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The commercialization of space is well underway, and as a result, Earth’s orbit is becoming ever more congested. The current number of active satellites in orbit stands at around 16,000, according to the European Space Agency( ESA), and this number is expected to jump close to 60,000 by 2035, Novaspace projects . While it’s not always given the recognition it deserves, space has fast become a critical infrastructure layer, underpinning nearly all systems that enable modern life as we know it. Therefore, it’s critical that a safe and clean operating landscape is maintained.

articles.title: Europe's Space Rider vehicle comes crashing down during drop test
articles.excerpt: The full-scale prototype of Europe's Space Rider orbiter failed to deploy its parachute during a drop test earlier this month, but ESA officials hope the setback won't delay progress toward its first…
articles.body: Europe has dropped the ball on the prototype for its first reusable spacecraft. Or, rather, the prototype itself was dropped — on purpose — but the outcome of its fall was not what engineers had hoped for. The incident occurred during an Oct. 6 drop test of the full-scale Space Rider model , from the European Space Agency (ESA). The robotic vehicle's initial drogue parachute deployed successfully, but its main parafoil detached during deployment, leaving the prototype unable to slow its descent before crashing into the ground, according to ESA officials. The cause of the failure remains under investigation.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media to 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium
articles.excerpt: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s sym…
articles.body: Members of the media are invited to join NASA at the 2026 von Braun Space Exploration Symposium from Monday, Oct. 26, to Wednesday, Oct. 28, at the University of Alabama in Huntsville. This year’s symposium is focused on humanity’s return to the Moon, sustainable lunar infrastructure, advanced space propulsion, and the evolving space workforce. Panels include discussions on Artemis II and III, space propulsion flash talks, building utilities and infrastructure for sustainable lunar operations, Moon base supply chain resilience, space nuclear technology, navigating the new NASA workforce, and engineering the future, featuring keynotes and awards presentations.
